# Sources and acknowledgements

<!-- GENERATED by pipeline/scripts/generateAttributions.ts — do not hand-edit.
     Regenerate after changing any manifest. -->

This engine's understanding of Scripture is not its own. Every theme it
recognises and every term it treats as evidence comes from people who spent
their lives explaining the Bible, and from communities who catalogued it. This
page names them.

**What ships and what does not.** The commentaries and expositions below are
read only at BUILD time. Their prose never enters the published artifact and is
never read at query time. What ships is a distillate: a term, a score, a count,
and a pointer back to who attested it. That distinction is deliberate, and it
is why sources whose *transcriptions* carry restrictions can still inform the
statistics without their text being redistributed.

**Attribution is a requirement here, not a courtesy.** OpenBible.info's data is
CC BY 4.0, which requires attribution in shipped output. This file is where
that obligation is met.

---

## Expositors

The verse-level evidence layer. A term is admitted only when **two or more of
these authors, independently, used it about the same verse** — which is what
separates the passage's theology from any one writer's habits of speech.

### Albert Barnes, Notes on the New Testament

- **Rights:** Public domain
- **Source:** <https://www.crosswire.org/ftpmirror/pub/sword/packages/rawzip/Barnes.zip>
- **Retrieved:** 2026-07-30
- **Checksum:** `9e8edc0333875c214124371b3862df118ad3a76ade7753cb2faeed3484615baf`

Public domain by age (Albert Barnes, 1798-1870; Notes published 1832-1851). Distributed by CrossWire as a SWORD module declaring DistributionLicense=Public Domain. The module records no TextSource, so the transcription's origin is unverified — admitted as public domain on the strength of the work's age and CrossWire's declaration, with that gap stated here rather than implied away. If a transcription claim ever surfaces, this manifest is where it gets recorded.

New Testament only, CHAPTER-blocked. Admitted to close the measured New Testament gap: with Clarke and Henry alone the NT sat at 84.2% while the OT reached 99.2%, and Mark at 47% was the worst-covered book in the Bible.

- **Checksum:** `ca3bdb6a04c0b717ee2faed71b432d58195db96f217f490ce6f7d9c36a2876f7`

Public domain by age (Karl Friedrich Keil 1807-1888, Franz Delitzsch 1813-1890; the 10-volume commentary published from 1864, English translation soon after). Distributed by CrossWire as a SWORD module declaring DistributionLicense=Public Domain with TextSource=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Biblical_commentary_the_Old_Testament. Deliberately NOT sourced from CCEL, so no transcription claim applies and this needs no reliance on the narrower reading recorded for mhc.

Old Testament only. Admitted specifically to close the measured gap: 9,835 verses had exactly one expositor and were therefore blocked by the corroboration rule, concentrated in Numbers, Genesis, 1-2 Chronicles, Deuteronomy, Ezekiel and Leviticus — the Pentateuch and historical books this commentary treats in most detail.

### Alexander Maclaren, Expositions of Holy Scripture: Psalms

- **Rights:** Public domain
- **Source:** <https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/7925/pg7925.txt>
- **Checksum:** `ca79e0cc06ef8dda8f7e139539f6db4e6782d3e0d5a6ebf94773b74b88e37c32`

Public domain. Project Gutenberg eBook #7925, released with no restrictions for US users; Maclaren died 1910 and the work was published in the 1900s. Gutenberg's proofread transcription carries no additional claim for US use.

Alignment tier 1: every exposition states its text explicitly (e.g. '--PSALM xxiii. 1-6.'), so passage attribution is parsing rather than inference. Gutenberg's PROOFREAD text is used deliberately in preference to Archive.org OCR of the same volume: 19th-century typography produces long-s and ligature garbage that would poison every term profile derived from it. Only distilled term/PMI pairs enter the artifact - the prose itself is never stored and never ships.

CCEL nonetheless asks permission for commercial republication of their own files, which is why treasury-of-david-* deliberately avoided them. ADMITTED HERE ON A NARROWER READING, decided by Jesse 2026-07-29: this artifact redistributes a term-statistics distillate — term, PMI, occurrence count and provenance — never the prose. Recorded in full rather than flattened to 'public_domain' so the judgment is auditable and so the difference from the Treasury decision is visible rather than looking like an inconsistency.

Second whole-Bible expositor, and therefore the source that first makes corroboration possible outside the Psalter. Written by SECTION, not by verse: the module stores one essay against every verse it covers, and the importer collapses those runs so the recorded span is the section Henry actually wrote about.

### C. H. Spurgeon, The Treasury of David, Vol. 1 (Psalms 1-26)

- **Rights:** Public domain
- **Source:** <https://archive.org/download/thetreasuryofdav01spuruoft/thetreasuryofdav01spuruoft_djvu.txt>
- **Checksum:** `38d558e4d70a4bf6d903114f85a49a4e82091728eca06a903aa99aa65ceed6d8`

Public domain by age (published 1869-1885; Spurgeon died 1892). Internet Archive scan from the University of Toronto set; IA asserts no additional copyright over the OCR text of a public-domain work.

Alignment tier 1, per-verse-heading shape: 'PSALM <roman>.' section headings with 'Verse N.--' commentary markers. OCR TEXT, not proofread - unlike the Maclaren volume, no Project Gutenberg edition of Treasury of David exists, so Internet Archive's OCR is the best cleanly-licensed option. Expect OCR noise (doubled spaces, mangled roman numerals, 'Title'->'Titte'); the parser rejects rather than guesses when a numeral is corrupted, because attaching commentary to the wrong psalm is a silent unrecoverable error. CCEL hosts a cleaner hand-corrected transcription but asks permission for commercial republication of THEIR files, so it is deliberately not used as the redistribution source - the text is public domain, that specific transcription is not unencumbered. Only distilled term/PMI pairs enter the artifact; the prose never ships.

## Declared for lineage only

These are not imported. They are recorded so that sources deriving from them
can declare that lineage, which keeps the engine from counting the same
scholarship twice as independent evidence.

- **LH editorial** — Authored for this dataset. LH holds all rights. Drafted with AI assistance offline and admitted by human review; no AI runs at query time.
- **Treasury of Scripture Knowledge** — Public domain by age (published 1830s). Not directly imported; declared so that sources deriving from it can express that lineage for correlation budgeting (G7).

---

## What is deliberately absent

- **Modern sermon libraries.** Several offer their material free of charge —
  Life.Church Open among them — but free of charge is not the same as licensed
  for redistribution. Life.Church's terms grant use "for your internal use and
  not for resale" and forbid exercising the granted rights "toward commercial
  advantage", which does not permit a publicly distributed artifact. Recorded
  here so the question does not have to be re-asked.
- **Copyrighted translations.** NIV, ESV and similar cannot be included. This
  has a visible consequence: a verse remembered in NIV wording may not match
  the public-domain text the engine searches.
- **CCEL's own transcription files**, where an alternative source exists. Where
  one does not, see the rights note on the affected source above.
